subject.title: fix(cron): warn on main heartbeat handoff ghost runs

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `cron.ghostRunWarningThresholdMs` and the `warnings` protocol field for this diagnostic, or keep the warning behind a fixed internal threshold?
rationale: The implementation adds a user-visible configuration key and protocol/client field for a heuristic diagnostic; repository policy requires a high bar and explicit compatibility-aware product judgment for new config surfaces.

options.title: Keep a fixed diagnostic threshold
options.body: Retain the scoped warning and run-history annotation but remove the new public threshold setting unless a concrete operator need requires tuning.

options.title: Approve the public setting
options.body: Accept the new threshold and protocol field as supported surfaces, with fresh rebased proof and clear upgrade/documentation coverage.

options.title: Pause for a stronger execution-health design
options.body: Defer this heuristic if maintainers want a confirmed delivery or agent-processing signal rather than a fast-run annotation.

recommendation.title: Keep a fixed diagnostic threshold
recommendation.body: Retain the scoped warning and run-history annotation but remove the new public threshold setting unless a concrete operator need requires tuning.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the main-session cron dispatch boundary that defines what a successful handoff means.
